checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in WY
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Commercial general contractor or the appropriate licensed trade contractor pulls each permit on the owner's behalf, and the contractor license information must appear on the application. For this job, the building permit is typically pulled by the GC, the electrical permit by the electrical contractor, and the mechanical permit by the mechanical contractor. Wyoming does not have a comprehensive statewide contractor licensing system, so Cheyenne may verify local registration and business credentials during intake.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City of Cheyenne Planning & Development
response_body.city_contractor_registration: Cheyenne does not appear to have a separate city contractor registration program documented in the provided city data, but because Wyoming licensing is locally controlled, verify current contractor credentials and business registration with Planning & Development before submitting. If the city requests contractor qualification documents, have your business license, insurance, and trade credentials ready.

common_mistakes: Submitting only a building permit and forgetting the separate electrical and mechanical permits for lifts, compressors, and radiant heat
Understating the project valuation on a commercial addition — Cheyenne uses valuation-based fees, so lowballing the value can delay approval and trigger corrections
Not coordinating slab thickness and anchor locations for vehicle lifts before the foundation pour
Starting steel erection or rough-in work before the permit is issued and posted on site
Failing to provide equipment cut sheets and load data for the lifts and compressor, which can stall plan review

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through the City of Cheyenne Planning & Development permit process tied to the building permit portal. Phone: (307) 637-6264. Expect 1-5 business days for standard inspection turnaround and allow extra time for commercial work. For a project this size, call ahead before pouring concrete and before covering any framing or rough-in work. If the portal requires separate trade inspection requests, submit building, electrical, and mechanical inspections individually and keep permit numbers handy.

inspections.description: Inspector checks footing depth, soil bearing, rebar placement, anchor bolts, slab thickening at lift locations, and any required frost-depth compliance before concrete is placed.
Inspector verifies steel framing, column connections, bracing, roof framing, wall framing, and load path for the addition before concealment.
inspections.timing: Before insulation, drywall, or wall/roof closure

inspections.description: Inspector checks feeder sizing, breaker protection, grounding and bonding, conduit/support, disconnects for lifts and equipment, receptacle placement, and any required GFCI/AFCI where applicable.
inspections.timing: Before walls are closed and before equipment is energized

inspections.description: Inspector verifies radiant heat piping or ducting, equipment clearances, venting, combustion air, gas piping if used, condensate drainage if applicable, and thermostat/control wiring.

Inspector checks that the addition is complete, equipment is installed and labeled, lifts are installed per manufacturer instructions, electrical covers are on, mechanical equipment is operational, and all life-safety items are in place.
inspections.timing: After all work is complete and equipment is ready for use

pro_tips: Bring a clean valuation breakdown with separate line items for shell, slab, electrical, mechanical, and lift equipment — it speeds up commercial fee review
For vehicle lifts, have the manufacturer installation instructions and anchor bolt requirements ready before the footing inspection
If the radiant heat is gas-fired, confirm venting and combustion air details early so the mechanical reviewer does not kick back the plans
Call Planning & Development before submitting to confirm whether they want the building, electrical, and mechanical permits filed together or as linked applications
Because Cheyenne charges a $50 Planning & Development review fee on all building permits, make sure that fee is included in your budget from the start

response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: Commercial additions can still be delayed by zoning setbacks, lot coverage, parking, access, and any overlay district rules. If the site is in a historic or special overlay area, exterior materials, height, and massing may need additional review. HOA restrictions are uncommon for a commercial auto repair site but private covenants can still affect exterior changes.
